Andrew Prokop is a senior politics correspondent at Vox, covering the White House, elections, and political scandals and investigations.
He’s worked at Vox since the site’s launch in 2014, and before that, he worked as a research assistant at the New Yorker’s Washington, DC, bureau.
CLEVELAND — It’s pretty disturbing to hear a large crowd at a major party convention repeatedly call for the jailing of the leader of the other major party.
It’s not just the crowd.
Three speakers _at the podium_ on the first day of the convention called for Hillary Clinton to be jailed.
Naturally, the crowd interrupted Christie _four_ times with the “lock her up” chant.
Indeed, the idea of sentencing Clinton to prison has been the only thing that’s really excited the crowd so far on this listless second day.
To me, all this seemed like a new crossing of a line and an ugly degradation of a norm in American politics.
Sentiments like these frequently bubble up from the grassroots of both parties.
Several liberal pundits and activists, and the occasional politician, called George W.
Bush a war criminal who deserved to be impeached.

The second annual Immersion Day event was filled with actionable insights and real-world examples for marketers.
At a conference built for marketing decision-makers rethinking how media works across the funnel, Amazon Ads sought to educate and inspire attendees on how to unlock the full value of its solutions.

The two-day Amazon Ads Immersion Day event in Culver City, California, brought senior media leaders together to learn actionable insights, receive real-world examples, and get direct access to the people and products that help power Amazon Ads.
Topics covered included their expanding portfolio of sports, growing array of artificial-intelligence capabilities, and case studies of successful customer campaigns.

Attendees were also treated to a rousing keynote address from Jay Shetty — the New York Times bestselling author, storyteller, and chief purpose officer at Calm — who talked about the importance of purpose in connecting brands with consumers.

The event was more than just programming, too: Each day ended with Immersion Fest, an outdoor experience with food, cocktails, live entertainment, and the chance to network with peers and industry partners.
